title:
Comment of Kathryn D. Dawson in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152093.txt
documents.text:
Kathryn D. Dawson, Homer, AK.
P-15423:

Dear FERC:

I am very strongly against P-15423, building a data center under Alaska’s Cook Inlet waters, for the following reasons:

1)	The “waste heat” generated by placing a huge, underwater, energy guzzling structure will not disappear into some black hole like a missing sock. The heat will enter a very fragile, already threatened ecosystem and disrupt the  marine biosphere from plankton all the way up to the protected Beluga Whales. The destruction of this habitat by introducing excessive heat energy into a delicately balanced ecosystem will also affect birds and humans who depend on the Cook Inlet waters for harvesting food, and tourism. It will also affect trees and vegetation, because the salmon carcasses, washed up or dragged out by bears from the rivers salmon spawn in, nourishes the soil. 
2)	Salmon species, an extremely important renewable resource for fishing, tourism and sustenance economies, are already experiencing harm from warming waters at the head of rivers, due to the climate disaster.
3)	Has a project this big ever been attempted? I believe the construction itself will tear up the Inlet’s underwater strata, scare off the Humpback Whales from an important feeding area, and create a major disruption from noise, boats, cranes and whatever else is introduced in this channel of Cook Inlet. The construction process itself will disrupt the migration and movements of important species. And then there is the disruption required whenever the data center or tidal generators need maintenance.
4)	Over 300 tidal generators? Have any studies been done on the damage this construction will cause? I’m all for alternative energy sources, but for Alaskans’ benefit, not to power a huge, destructive data center which will have little or no benefit for people living on the Kenai Peninsula or Alaska. And Alaskans are going to be the ones paying the huge electric bill when the tide is out and the data centers need to gobble energy constantly. Alaskans’ energy bills are already too high, and will become higher when President Trump restarts the Iran War. Alaskan taxpayers cannot afford to pay DeepGreen’s energy bill, especially when a war that will destroy the energy economy and drastically increase gas and diesel prices is undergone. This is a bad time to add an energy-gobbling structure for Alaskans to pay for.
5)	There will be corrosion, which will release copper and other poisonous minerals into the water, further damaging the ecosystem. If sonar testing is used to map the underwater surface, whales and other cetaceans’ hearing will be destroyed, and many will die.

In conclusion, P-15423 will drastically harm or destroy an important, renewable resource wildlife and humans depend on in the Cook Inlet and surrounding areas. Alaskans’ economic viability and dependance on food resources will be negatively impacted by this project, which will mostly benefit outside, corporate interests who will be unable and unwilling to pay the external costs of building their data center in Cook Inlet. It will be Alaskans who end up paying with their diminished wallets, a diminished or destroyed ecotourism and fishing industry, and the pollution, noise and disruption of such a huge project. I strongly recommend DeepGreen’s Cook Inlet data center not be approved.
Thank-you, Kathryn Dawson.
